title: Primitive Instances inherit a base class of operational logic from the Core Atlas, and changes to it propagate automatically
content:
Each of the eight Distribution Reward Instances carries the identical Routine Protocol wording (A.6.1.1.4.2.5.1.2.1.2.1 and siblings): "This Instance inherits the base class of operational logic defined in A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1 - Routine Protocol, subject to the qualifications specified in A.2.2.9.1.2.1.3.3.1 - Near-Term Process." It then states the consequence explicitly: "**Modifications to the base operational logic automatically propagate to this Instance.**"

The Atlas is using class inheritance as a governance construct. The Core Atlas holds the base class; each Agent Instance is a subclass that, by default, contains no overriding code at all. A single edit at A.2.2.9.1.2.4.1 changes how every Distribution Reward Instance across every Agent operates.

This is enormously efficient and it creates a real tension with the Root Edit process. A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2 requires a 1% proposer, a Facilitator alignment review, and a token holder poll to change the Skybase Artifact — yet the operational logic actually governing Skybase's distribution program can change through a Core Atlas edit that SKYBASE holders do not vote on. The Agent's autonomy covers the *text of its Artifact*, not the behaviour inherited into it.

The defence is that inheritance flows only downward from the constitutional layer, and that Agents cannot violate the Core Atlas anyway (A.6.1.1.4.2.2.2.2.1.2.1.6), so propagation merely keeps Agents current with rules they were already bound by. The cost is that the Skybase Artifact is not self-contained: reading it tells you what Skybase decided, not what Skybase does.

Each Instance also flags this as provisional — "in future iterations of the Skybase Artifact, a version of the full process definition customized to Skybase will be included herein" — so the current total reliance on inherited logic is explicitly a starting state.
description: Every Distribution Reward Instance states that modifications to the Sky Core base protocol propagate without an Agent Artifact edit
